items.title: Steve Turré interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 29, 2021
items.q: But I know I played with Dizzy and he would show me some tunes just at the sound check or in the dressing room

ctx.x: So music for you, does it have a spiritual connection of a sort?

More than of a sort, it goes back to the essence of life. It’s a reflection of that. Whatever the life condition is it comes out in your music. You can’t fake that. You know we’ve all heard young students say — they’ve got a saxophone and they’ve got great fingers and they can run all the scales. I haven’t really heard any of them could play “Giant Steps” through the keys. But there’s probably a few. But they’re not playing any music. It sounds like they’re playing the computer or something. It sounds like a…

Okay. Was there a particular artist, you mentioned John Coltrane a little bit ago, and I wonder if there was a particular artist that you started listening to that was an on-spot example of what you’re talking about with the spirit, not just the technique and the instrumental prowess, but the spirit behind it?
